HONOLULU. Dec. l6 tAP).-
Two obsolete aircraft carriers
and a Dutch tugboat were
tossed helplessly today in the
fury of a Pacific storm south
of Midway Island. Four ships
sped to their rescue.


High seas broke tow lines
from the tug Elbe to the two
small United States carriers,
Guadalcanal and Mission Bay.


Then one of the broken tow
lines fouled in the Elbe's pro-
peller and she. too, was helpless.


The Navy said the Elbe car
ried Is crewmen and a skeleton
crew Of eight men was on each
of the World War II carriers.
The carriers were being towed
to Japan for scrapping.


The destroyer Richard S.
Edwards was nearest the scene.
about $50 miles south of Mid
way and 1900 miles west of
Honolulu. The DESTROYER was
expected to reach the area late
today.


The carrier Bon Homme
Richard and the Navy tugboat
Moctobi were ordered to the
scene. The Dutch tug Clyde,
also towing small carriers to
Japan. left her tows at Homo
lulu and set out for the distress
area.

Mites are a major problem
this summer on many ever
greens, chiefly juniper, hem
lock, spruce, arborvitae and
lockwood. Already many trees
are turning bronze or dusty
yellow.


These tiny spider-like pests
critically injure evergreens,
oaks, poplars and sycamores
by sucking vital plant juices.


There are many species of
mites-spider mites, red mites,
spruce mites. They attack
sunny areas Of a tree, multiply
rapidly. overlap generations so
that eggs, nymphs and adults
all may be present at the same
time. Some work the bottom
side Of the leaves, spinning
gossamer webs; other prefer
the topside.


This year mites seem more
abundant than ever and began
deSpoiling trees earlier than
usual. They can be controlled
by spraying with a good miti-
eide such as kelthane. Spray
ing priced evergreens several
times from now until Indian
summer is recommended.

years ago. Scientists are now
eagerly awaiting the final re-
suits of this falls census, hop

The whooper once ranged

bon Society, in the National

tiers drove the huge white

the Aransas National Wildlife
Refuge was created in 1887 to
protect them in their winter

know where the birds nested

during that crucial period.


The first clue came in 1852

north of Great Slave Lake in
the Canadian Northwest Ter
ritories. After three more years
of searching, Mr.. Allen and two
companions from the United
States Fish and Wildlife Serv-
ice finally reached the nesting
grounds in an isolated region
of Canada's enormous Wood
Buffalo National Park.


Committing between winter
and summer homes, the birds
travel over Texas, Oklahoma,
Kansas, Nebraska, North and
South Dakota, Montana, SaS-
Satchewan and Alberta. CruiS-
ing at As miles per hour, they
cover about 200 miles a day de-
spite many food stops. The
young return over the same
<oute with their families, ar

or early November.

roosting ponds just before SUM-
up, and stroll along a favorite
route, looking for crabs, other
crustaceans, worms, fish, mol
!usks, and a few vegetable items
such as acronS. After breakfast,
they preen. The rest of the day
is spent alternately feeding and
preening. At night they ramble
back to the ponds where they
sleep.

were greeted with Kisses and

dozen campus police. responded.

As Washington begins pulling
its woolens out Of the moth
balls. residents of McAllen.
Harlingen and Brownsville are
preparing for q shirtsleeve win
ter along streets lined with
palm trees.


The temperature during
January viii average so degrees
in the 75-mile strip paralleling
the Rio Grande and the Texas
border with Mexico. Many MD
western refugees from snow
and winter will flock down to
the Rio Grande beginning in
December.


The valley Of the Rio
Grande is Just beginning to be-
come popular with vacationers
from Washington, New York
and New England.


They are finding In 1t the
oleanders blooming in profusion
among palm trees, the mild and
sunny climate-deep in the
heart Of Texas-that they have
liked In Florida and southern
California. n


The Valley, however. has not
yet succumbed to the f1amboy-
ancy that are the hallmarks Of
Miami or southern California.
on the Yankee-or Texas-side
Of the border things are quiet
and comfortable. Cafeterias
and motels are more plentiful
than elaborate restaurants and
hotels in the string of towns
that stretch for 81 miles from
Brownsville and Harlingen
along the palm Lined Main
Street" Of the Valley-U. S.
Highway 83-to McAllen, Edin-
burgh and Mission. !,


Souvenir shops. night clubs
and colorful plazaS mark the
towns on the Mexican side Of
the border. There are bull fights
on some Sundays in Matamoros
and Reynosa; some tourists
drive on further northwest to
storied Laredo and cross to
Nuevo Laredo for the bullfights,
which are held there each Sun
day.


Looks Deceiving


The looks of restaurants are
deceiving. The frame building
that is Joe's Place on the border
side of Reynosa's outskirts
houses a clean restaurant
popular with tourists and Nc
Allen residents alike - where
you can get a nine-course din
ner featuring quail or pheasant
for about what supper costs in
a good Washington cafeteria.


The New Orleans Bar in
Nuevo Laredo is similarly
deceptive. Tourists should be
wary, nevertheless. for equally
dumpy exteriors house reStau-
rants in which the interiors are
nothing to rave about either.


AT night the central plaza in
each Mexican city is alive with
people, music, and light. The
retail shops fan out along the
streets from the central plaza.
around which you can. also see
the towns most interesting
churches and their modern
municipal government build
ings. H


By design or tradition, the
hours kept by most Mexican
tourist shops coincide with
tourist hours. Whether they
close for midday siesta or not,
most shops remain open till
8 or Q pm, some later than
that.


Leather purses. slippers and
belts are good buys. in plentiful
variety, at the shops on both
Mexican and United States
sides of the border.


From downtown Brownsville
it's Just a short walk across
the international bridge into
Matamoros. Most people drive.
or take the bus, past lovely
stucco homes in pastel colors
the better ones offering OBJ
servers q modern expression OF
the classic Spanish architecture
with its central patios, outer
fences, moorish arches and
elaborate metal grillwork. From |
McAllen, it's dozen minutes
drive, or ride on the bus,
through the border village Of
Hidalgo across the bridge into
Reynosa. Laredo and Nuevo
Laredo, just northwest Of the
valley, are virtually twin cities
in their closeness, but two diff
ferent worlds in their civic
appearances.


Crossing Is Easy


There's no problem for tour
lists about going in and out of
Mexico. Thousands of visitors,
residents and workers make
the round trip every day. You'll
need only proof Of citizenship
"a birth certificate, baptismal
certificate or draft card.


It's not always quiet on the
Texas side Of the border dur

tests and dancing. Brownsville
has its historic Charro Days,
in February. The whole val
ley joins in the Citrus Festival,

THE FACTS: The so-called 1925 set of regu-

been argued that the United States Public

and that if this imported milk meets United

should be good enough for this area.
Please don't let yourself stand pat" by accepting
such assertions that gloss the important issues
involved.


Don't let yourself be influenced by anyone who
wants change made in present regulations so that
milk of inferior quality to that which you now

metropolitan area.


Don't let cOmplacency lead you to be silent when

ences between your District of Columbia milk reg
ulations and U.SPH Standards"

Your present laws provide for enforcement in
the field and at the dairy. They are not recon-
mendations, points of order" or simple procedure
plans They are health laws with teeth in them,
and every now and then they really bite.


The United States Public Health Service Stand
ards are merely that-standards. The Federal
Government supplies them to any city or area
that wishes to use them. They are minimum
standards. They provide for less frequent inspec-
ton in many instances and do not provide any
machinery for enforcement That is local mat
ter. AS an example of how these standards are
inadequate in their present form, one has only to
look at the milk health laws in st. Louis and Chi
cago. While these laws are based on United States
Public Health Service standards to an extent,
these cities had to adopt higher standards and

Alexandria, in a move that is
capturing wide attention, has ex-
tended It's school-testing program
this year to the lowest possible
age level.


The results, confirming what the
city's school officials said had been
worrying them for long time,
showed that a surprisingly large
number Of 6-year-old children are
too immature for first-grade work.


So Alexandria school officials
decided to do something about it..


Testing the intelligence and
mental capabilities Of school chill
dren is a long-accepted practice
everywhere. Like many, other
school systems, Alexandria tests
all its school pupils periodically to
determine their school potential.
But it went one step further this
year. Preschool children were
given mental maturity tests to find
out whether they were ready to
enter the first grade.


Test results showed that 1903 of
the city's 1859 potential first
graders were incapable of taking
regular school work, Officials said.
Under the new plan they were
not permitted to enroll for classes.


Instead these children will at
tend new readiness centers" set
to open this week in four of Alex
andria's elementary schools. There
they will prepare, under the guild
ance Of special teachers, to enter
the first grade next year.

VENICE. Fla, Oct. 16 (AP).
The menacing red tide has
left its mark of dead fish on
beaches here and biologists
predict more of the smelly
creatures will wash ashore.


Thick patches of rotting fish
washed ashore along a Is
mile front yesterday and
brought sitting fumes to this
area.


City Inspector Guy Kerwood
said crews have removed sew
eral truckloads of fish from
the clty-owned beach but "gas
fumes were so strong the
workers had to quit several
times to get fresh air."


Acid fumes which accom-
pany red tide can cause irrita-
ton to the eyes, lungs, skin
and noses of humans.


Red tide is a marine micro
organism which becomes con-
centrated and fatal to fish under
certain weather conditions. The
organisms give off a toxic sub
lance, turning the water a
rusty color.

resort. Giants Of the motel field

winter visitors are the Sea-
scape, Stowaway, Westward Ho,
French Quarter and Sandyhill.


During the winter months

ers. travelling from New York,

city council tend to discount

ing in recent years have in

heating.

pool.
